newsitem.title: UK: Poll shows strong support for British rabies law.
newsitem.headline: Poll shows strong support for British rabies law.

text.p: Nearly two-thirds of Britons support a strict quarantine law designed to keep out rabies, despite growing pressure for change, an opinion poll said on Friday.
The NOP poll showed 64 percent percent of people questioned favoured keeping the law, which requires pets brought into the country from abroad to be kept in quarantine for six months.
Thirty-six percent said they would prefer a system of guarding against the disease with vaccinations and pets' passports, proposed by many vets and animal rights groups.

Britain is one of the few countries in the world where rabies has been wiped out. But opponents of the present law say it is cruel and expensive and increases the risk that rabies will be brought into Britain because it encourages people to smuggle in their pets.
Since 1946, nearly 200,000 pets have been through quarantine but only 15 developed rabies while in the six-month isolation period. In the last 25 years there have been only two suspected cases.
